request.spec:
The sheets must be kept completely separate. People I add to one sheet must never appear on
another sheet.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for this implementation's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheets must be kept completely separate. People I add to one sheet must never appear on
another sheet.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Sheets are now fully separate. `bin/e2e` passes: the new isolation test passes, and so does the replay of all 18 earlier test fixtures.

**The cause:** a person's id was shared by every sheet, so two sheets could never each have their own person 1. Edits also looked people up by id alone, without checking the sheet.

**The fix:** each sheet now numbers its own people, and everything that finds or changes a person also looks at which sheet it's on.
- **Database:** a new migration, `V7__person_sheet_local_id.sql`, adds a per-sheet `local_id` that must be unique within a sheet. Existing people keep their current numbers. The old id stays as a hidden internal key, which patron links still use.
- **Server:** the API now shows each person's per-sheet id. Adding someone gives them the next free number on that sheet. Editing someone (`PATCH /api/people/{id}?sheet=…`) only finds people on that sheet, and patrons can only be chosen from the same sheet.
- **Front end:** every edit (alpha, beta, gamma, patrons, the Edit form) now sends the open sheet.
- **Test seeding and read-back:** fixture ids are stored as per-sheet ids, and patron links are matched within their own sheet.

I also tried it against the running app: two sheets each got their own person 1, and an edit sent to a sheet that didn't have that id returned 404.

One thing to know: the `ALPHA_CHANGED id=… from=… to=…` audit record keeps its existing format, so `id` is now the per-sheet id. The record doesn't say which sheet, so the same id on two sheets looks identical in the audit file. Adding the sheet would change a format that tests rely on, so I left it as is.
